findings.title: `import()` expressions in object literal are still evaluated eagerly at module load
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry of `appStore` is written as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` instead of a function like `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because the `import(...)` calls are property value expressions on the object literal, JavaScript evaluates every dynamic import immediately when `@calcom/app-store` is imported, loading all 28 app modules upfront rather than on demand when a specific app is accessed.

findings.title: `async` callback in `.forEach` pushes `deleteEvent` promises after `Promise.all` has already run
findings.body: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 458-470), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` uses an `async` callback inside `.forEach`. Because `.forEach` does not await the returned promises, execution immediately continues past the loop and reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) before `getCalendar` or ` calendar.deleteEvent` has resolved and before anything is pushed into `apiDeletes`. As a result, recurring calendar event deletions are not awaited (and in serverless environments may be terminated before completing), and any errors they throw become unhandled promise rejections.
